Hi front-counter team,
Animal welfare came up mid-afternoon, so just a quick note

Please treat every live-animal case as a priority and keep the handoff calm, clear, and fast. If a traveler arrives with a carrier, check that the booking details match the animal paperwork before anything moves forward, and escalate any mismatch at once. Safety takes priority over speed in every journey, and we need that message reflected in every interaction. The passenger coordinator will keep guiding the required steps, but the front counter must be ready to answer basic process questions without delay.

If there is any sign of distress, temperature risk, or carrier damage, stop the normal flow and call for support immediately. Anika Davis or Yuki Schneider may ask about alternate arrangements, and Basil may also be mentioned in a case note, so please stay focused and avoid assumptions. For incident handling, <<FACT F109>> If the traveler asks about filing after an escape in transit, <<FACT F120>> Keep those details out of the conversation unless the inserted guidance is being shared, and do not improvise timing or payout language.

Please also remember to document what you see in plain terms, keep the tone steady, and hand the case to the senior coordinator as soon as the desk is clear enough to do so. We need every team member aligned today so no traveler is left waiting for the next step. Thank you for moving quickly and staying careful.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
